Chapter 10: Sustaining a Multiplier Culture—Scaling Beyond the Individual.
You know, it’s amazing what one strong leader can do. But if you really want to see lasting change, the magic happens when multiplying behaviors become part of the very fabric of your organization.
So, how do you actually make that shift from a few Multipliers to a true Multiplier culture? Let’s walk through some practical ways you can help this approach take root, not just with individuals, but across your entire team.
First up—think about how you hire and promote. Instead of just looking for technical skills or people with the loudest voices, look for those who naturally attract talent, encourage debate, and empower others. Imagine a workplace where the folks moving up are the ones who help everyone shine, not just themselves.
Next, try weaving Multiplier practices right into your daily processes. Picture regular debate forums, peer coaching, and giving people true ownership over their projects—all of these can become part of your normal workflow. It’s about making the five disciplines a natural part of how things get done.
And don’t forget to celebrate your Multipliers! When someone truly lives out those five disciplines, make it visible—recognize and reward them. It sends a powerful message about what really matters around here, and it inspires others to follow their lead.
Of course, developing these skills takes time and support. That’s why offering workshops, coaching, and resources can make a real difference. Give everyone—at every level—the chance to grow as a Multiplier.
Peer accountability is another key ingredient. Create spaces where people can give each other honest feedback, both on multiplying and diminishing behaviors. When folks feel safe to speak up and help each other improve, the whole team gets stronger.
Here’s a real-world example: some organizations set up a “Multiplier Roundtable.” Leaders gather regularly to share stories about how they’re applying the disciplines, talk through challenges, and help each other grow. It’s a simple idea, but it keeps the conversation alive and the culture moving in the right direction.
Now, sustaining a Multiplier culture isn’t a one-and-done thing. It takes ongoing attention. You’ll want to keep an eye out for accidental diminishing—those little habits or reactions that might hold your team back without you even realizing it. Encourage regular reflection and open discussions about how your leadership styles are affecting everyone’s ability to contribute and grow.
Over time, as multiplying becomes the norm, you’ll notice something incredible: engagement goes up, innovation takes off, and performance gets stronger. And it doesn’t happen because of just a few superstar leaders—it happens because everyone feels empowered to bring their best, every single day.
